title: Evaluate Postfix Expression
description:
Evaluate an expression written in postfix (Reverse Polish) notation, where every operator comes after its two operands. For example 2 3 + 4 * means (2 + 3) * 4 = 20. Use a stack: push numbers, and for an operator pop the right operand, then the left operand, and push the result.

  • Tokens are separated by single spaces.
  • Operators: + - * /. A token is an operator only if it is exactly one of these characters; tokens like -3 are negative numbers.
  • Division is integer division that truncates toward zero (e.g. -7 / 2 = -3). No division by zero occurs.
  • The expression is always valid and has at most 2000 tokens.

Input

A single line containing the postfix expression.

Output

Print the value of the expression.

Example

Input:

2 3 + 4 *

Output:

20

title: Infix to Postfix Conversion
description:
Convert an infix expression to postfix notation using the shunting-yard algorithm (an operator stack).

  • Operands are single letters or single digits.
  • Operators: + - (lowest), * /, and ^ (highest).
  • + - * / are left-associative; ^ is right-associative, so a^b^c becomes abc^^.
  • Parentheses may appear. The expression is valid, has no spaces and at most 1000 characters.

Input

A single line containing the infix expression.

Output

Print the postfix expression with no spaces (parentheses do not appear in the output).

Example

Input:

a+b*c

Output:

abc*+

title: Infix Expression Evaluator
description:
Evaluate an arithmetic expression written in ordinary infix notation. Use two stacks (numbers and operators) or a recursive-descent parser — do not use eval.

  • The expression contains non-negative integers, the operators + - * /, parentheses and arbitrary spaces.
  • * and / bind tighter than + and -; operators of the same precedence are evaluated left to right.
  • / is integer division that truncates toward zero (-7 / 2 = -3, 7 / 2 = 3).
  • There is no unary minus, and no division by zero occurs. Length ≤ 15000 characters.

Input

A single line containing the expression.

Output

Print the integer value of the expression.

Example

Input:

2 + 3 * (4 - 1)

Output:

11

title: Next Greater Element
description:
For every element of an array, find the first element to its right that is strictly greater than it. If there is none, the answer for that position is -1. A monotonic stack solves this in linear time.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000
  • -105 ≤ values ≤ 105

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.

Output

Print n space-separated integers: the next greater element of each position.

Example

Input:

4
4 5 2 25

Output:

5 25 25 -1
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
res = [-1] * n
st = []
for i in range(n):
    while st and a[st[-1]] < a[i]:
        res[st.pop()] = a[i]
    st.append(i)
print(" ".join(map(str, res)))

title: Daily Temperatures
description:
Given the temperature of each day, compute for each day how many days you have to wait until a strictly warmer day. If no warmer day follows, the answer is 0.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 4000
  • 30 ≤ temperature ≤ 100

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains n temperatures.

Output

Print n space-separated integers.

Example

Input:

8
73 74 75 71 69 72 76 73

Output:

1 1 4 2 1 1 0 0
solution:
n = int(input())
t = list(map(int, input().split()))
res = [0] * n
st = []
for i in range(n):
    while st and t[st[-1]] < t[i]:
        j = st.pop()
        res[j] = i - j
    st.append(i)
print(" ".join(map(str, res)))

title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
description:
A histogram has n bars of width 1 and the given heights, standing side by side. Find the area of the largest rectangle that fits completely inside the histogram (the rectangle must be axis-aligned and rest on the base line).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3500
  • 0 ≤ height ≤ 9999
  • Checking every pair of borders is too slow for the largest inputs; use a monotonic stack to find, for each bar, how far it can extend left and right.

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains the n heights.

Output

Print the maximum rectangle area.

Example

Input:

6
2 1 5 6 2 3

Output:

10
solution:
n = int(input())
h = list(map(int, input().split())) + [0]
st = []
best = 0
for i in range(n + 1):
    start = i
    while st and st[-1][1] >= h[i]:
        idx, height = st.pop()
        best = max(best, height * (i - idx))
        start = idx
    st.append((start, h[i]))
print(best)

title: Min Stack Simulation
description:
Simulate a stack that can also report its minimum element. Process the commands in order:

  • push x — push integer x.
  • pop — remove the top element. Prints nothing, unless the stack is empty, in which case print EMPTY.
  • top — print the top element, or EMPTY.
  • min — print the smallest element currently in the stack, or EMPTY.

Every operation should take constant time (keep the running minimum alongside each element).

  • 1 ≤ Q ≤ 3000, -109 ≤ x ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains Q, followed by Q command lines.

Output

Print the output of each top/min command, and of each pop on an empty stack, one per line.

Example

Input:

7
push 5
push 3
min
push 7
top
pop
min

Output:

3
7
3

title: Queue Using Two Stacks
description:
Implement a FIFO queue using only two stacks (an in stack for new elements and an out stack you refill only when it is empty). Process the commands:

  • enqueue x — add x to the back (prints nothing).
  • dequeue — remove and print the front element, or print EMPTY.
  • front — print the front element without removing it, or EMPTY.
  • size — print the number of elements.
  • 1 ≤ Q ≤ 3000

Input

The first line contains Q, followed by Q command lines.

Output

One output line for every dequeue, front and size command.

Example

Input:

6
enqueue 1
enqueue 2
front
dequeue
size
dequeue

Output:

1
1
1
2

title: Simplify Unix Path
description:
Given an absolute Unix-style path, print its simplified canonical form:

  • The path starts with a single /; directory names are separated by single slashes.
  • Multiple consecutive slashes count as one slash.
  • . means the current directory and is removed.
  • .. moves up one directory; going up from the root stays at the root.
  • Any other name, including ... or .hidden, is a regular directory name.
  • No trailing slash (except the root itself, which is /).
  • 1 ≤ length ≤ 3000; the path contains letters, digits, ., _ and /.

Input

A single line containing the path.

Output

Print the simplified path.

Example

Input:

/home//foo/

Output:

/home/foo

title: Asteroid Collision
description:
Asteroids move along a line. The absolute value is the size, the sign is the direction (positive = moving right, negative = moving left), and all move at the same speed. When a right-moving asteroid meets a left-moving one, the smaller one explodes; if both have the same size, both explode. Two asteroids moving in the same direction never meet. Print the state after all collisions.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 4000
  • 1 ≤ |value| ≤ 1000, no zeros

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains n non-zero integers in order from left to right.

Output

Print the surviving asteroids from left to right separated by single spaces, or EMPTY if none survive.

Example

Input:

3
5 10 -5

Output:

5 10

title: Remove K Digits
description:
Remove exactly k digits from a non-negative integer (given as a string) so that the remaining number is as small as possible. The relative order of the remaining digits does not change. Leading zeros of the result are dropped; if nothing (or only zeros) remains, the answer is 0.

  • 1 ≤ number of digits ≤ 10000; the number has no leading zeros unless it is 0.
  • 0 ≤ k ≤ number of digits
  • A greedy monotonic stack gives a linear solution.

Input

The first line contains the number. The second line contains k.

Output

Print the smallest possible result.

Example

Input:

1432219
3

Output:

1219
solution:
num = input().strip()
k = int(input())
st = []
for d in num:
    while k and st and st[-1] > d:
        st.pop()
        k -= 1
    st.append(d)
if k:
    st = st[:-k]
res = "".join(st).lstrip("0")
print(res if res else "0")

title: Stock Span
description:
The span of a stock's price on a given day is the number of consecutive days, ending with that day and going backwards, on which the price was less than or equal to that day's price. Compute the span for every day.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 4000
  • 1 ≤ price ≤ 1000

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains the n prices.

Output

Print the n spans separated by single spaces.

Example

Input:

7
100 80 60 70 60 75 85

Output:

1 1 1 2 1 4 6
solution:
n = int(input())
p = list(map(int, input().split()))
st = []
res = []
for i in range(n):
    while st and p[st[-1]] <= p[i]:
        st.pop()
    res.append(i + 1 if not st else i - st[-1])
    st.append(i)
print(" ".join(map(str, res)))

description:
Given a string of ( and ), find the longest contiguous substring that is a valid (well-formed) parentheses string. Report its length and the 0-based index where it starts. If several longest substrings exist, report the leftmost one.

  • 1 ≤ length ≤ 15000
  • Checking every substring is far too slow; a stack of indices (with a sentinel for the last unmatched position) finds the answer in one pass.

Input

A single line containing the string.

Output

Print two integers separated by a space: the maximum length and the start index. If there is no valid substring, print 0 -1.

Example

Input:

)()())

Output:

4 1

title: Count Two-Sum Pairs
description:
Count the pairs of positions (i, j) with i < j such that a[i] + a[j] = T. Equal values at different positions form different pairs.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3500
  • -500 ≤ a[i] ≤ 500, -1000 ≤ T ≤ 1000
  • Checking all pairs is too slow for the largest cases; count with a hash map of values seen so far.

Input

The first line contains n and T. The second line contains n integers.

Output

Print the number of pairs.

Example

Input:

5 6
1 5 7 -1 5

Output:

3
solution:
n, T = map(int, input().split())
seen = {}
count = 0
for x in map(int, input().split()):
    count += seen.get(T - x, 0)
    seen[x] = seen.get(x, 0) + 1
print(count)

Output

title: Subarrays with Exactly K Distinct
description:
Count the contiguous subarrays that contain exactly k different values.

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 5000
  • 1 ≤ a[i] ≤ 100
  • Enumerating all subarrays is too slow. Hint: exactly(k) = atMost(k) − atMost(k−1), and atMost can be counted with a sliding window and a frequency map.

Input

The first line contains n and k. The second line contains the n integers.

Output

Print the number of subarrays with exactly k distinct values.

Example

Input:

5 2
1 2 1 2 3

Output:

7

title: LRU Cache Simulation
description:
Simulate a Least Recently Used cache with a fixed capacity. Commands:

  • get key — print the value stored for key, or -1 if it is not in the cache. A successful get makes the key the most recently used.
  • put key value — insert or update the key, making it the most recently used. If inserting a new key while the cache is full, first evict the least recently used key.
  • 1 ≤ capacity ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ Q ≤ 3000
  • Keys and values are positive integers ≤ 105.

Input

The first line contains capacity and Q, followed by Q command lines.

Output

Print the result of each get on its own line.

Example

2 9

get 1

put 4 4

get 4

Output:

1
-1

4

title: Distinct Values in Every Window
description:
For every window of k consecutive elements, count how many different values it contains. Maintain a frequency map while sliding the window instead of recounting each window.

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 5000
  • -104 ≤ a[i] ≤ 104

Input

The first line contains n and k. The second line contains the n integers.

Output

Print n - k + 1 integers separated by single spaces: the distinct counts of the windows from left to right.

Example

Input:

7 4
1 2 1 3 4 2 3

Output:

3 4 4 3

title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
description:
For every contiguous subarray take its minimum element; print the sum of all these minimums modulo 1000000007.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 4000
  • 1 ≤ a[i] ≤ 9999
  • Enumerating all n(n+1)/2 subarrays is too slow for the largest inputs. For each element count how many subarrays have it as their minimum using monotonic stacks (careful with equal values: count each subarray exactly once).

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains the n integers.

Output

Print the sum modulo 1000000007.

Example

Input:

4
3 1 2 4

Output:

17
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
M = 10 ** 9 + 7
left = [0] * n
right = [0] * n
st = []
for i in range(n):
    while st and a[st[-1]] > a[i]:
        st.pop()
    left[i] = i - st[-1] if st else i + 1
    st.append(i)
st = []
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    while st and a[st[-1]] >= a[i]:
        st.pop()
    right[i] = st[-1] - i if st else n - i
    st.append(i)
print(sum(a[i] * left[i] * right[i] for i in range(n)) % M)

title: Longest Zero-Sum Subarray
description:
Find the longest contiguous subarray whose elements sum to exactly 0. If several have the maximum length, choose the leftmost one. Store the first index at which each prefix sum appears in a hash map.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 4000
  • -1000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains the n integers.

Output

Print the length and the 0-based start index separated by a space. If no zero-sum subarray exists print 0 -1.

Example

Input:

8
15 -2 2 -8 1 7 10 23

Output:

5 1
